office_does: The auditor runs elections and voter registration, records deeds and other documents, issues licenses, and keeps the county's accounts and annual financial statement.
race_blurb: A 2022 rematch: Sheilah Crider, auditor since 2008 and now running as an Independent, led the four-way primary with 39.7%, and Barbara Fuller (Prefers Democratic Party), a compliance and audit professional, was second with 28.0%. Local coverage frames it as continuity against change, with office staffing as the main issue.

candidates.summary: Coupeville compliance and audit professional, former police officer and member of the county Civil Service Commission, making her second run for auditor; endorsed by the Island County Democrats.
highlights: Lists 25+ years in regulatory compliance, auditing and operational leadership [S1]
Wants to modernize the office and find out why the chief accountant post stayed vacant for nearly a year [S3]
Would look for 'more cost-effective and sustainable ways' to run the office [S3]
Says she will not 'clean house' and would start with an assessment drawing on staff input [S2]
Expects the county will need a new elections office at some point [S2]

spending.basis: Pledges strong financial oversight and more cost-effective operations and has criticized weak handling of an audit finding; she also expects a new elections office will be needed.

experience.basis: Never elected and running a second time as the change candidate against an 18-year incumbent, with a long professional auditing career behind her.

candidates.summary: Island County Auditor since her 2008 appointment and a state-certified election administrator, formerly an Oak Harbor city councilmember; running as an Independent after running as a Republican in 2022.
highlights: Auditor for 18 years, after 10 years on the Oak Harbor City Council [S1]
Says the office's 'policies, practices and procedures have stood the test of time' [S2]
Says salary limits hiring and wants funding for a backup employee [S3]
A judge upheld her 2024 mask mandate in the ballot-counting room [S5]
Plans stronger election security ahead of the 2028 presidential election [S2]

spending.basis: Blames limited salary money for staffing gaps and seeks funding for an added backup position and for an observer space.

experience.basis: Incumbent for 18 years, running on the office's record and continuity, after a decade on a city council.
